_note: The visor TERRAIN GHOST in the cockpit, ONE run for three strengths. The player is seated in the cockpit view at 1500 m over the west of the island (map x -6 km, z +10 km), heading west (270) at 180 m/s toward the massif whose peaks stand 1.3 to 1.6 km (map x -18..-12 km, z +6..+14 km): in 16 s it flies about 3 km, never closer than 4 km to the peaks, and every 320 m cell of the 10 km grid around it has real ground heights (sea at the coast, thinned to every fourth line; ground higher than 150 m under the aircraft, here the massif, in the caution colour at double strength). After 8 s the ghost has faded in; TerrainGhostAutomation.Configure sets the strength IN MEMORY ONLY (the saved TerrainGhost setting is never written; restore gives it back, cfg ghost_restored.saved false): ghost-default is the saved default (0.35, 'barely there'), ghost-full is strength 1, ghost-off is strength 0 (nothing may be drawn: compare it with the other two). Each Configure result is stored: supportedMap (a baked heightfield was found), materialFound (the line shader exists), vertexCount, lastRebuildMs, fade, cautionVertices. The checks assert those and that the Unity log has no Exception; nothing asserts the pixels, that is read off the three captures. The cockpit interior is drawn by a second (overlay) camera over the main one, so in the cockpit view the ghost is drawn on THAT camera (squeezed into its 5 m of depth at the same screen position) and shows over the cockpit's own opaque parts too: ghost_default.camera must read cockpit, and the captures should show the lines over the dashboard.
name: terrain-ghost
description: Visor terrain ghost in one cockpit run: the default strength, strength 1 and strength 0 over real ground.
